title: Indistinguishability of single Raman photons from single atoms
authors: Pascal Baumgart, Max Bergerhoff, Jürgen Eschner
abstract: We theoretically investigate the indistinguishability of single photons generated from single trapped $^{40}$Ca$^+$ ions in a Raman scattering process driven by few-nanosecond excitation pulses. Of particular interest is how spontaneous decay back to the initial state affects Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) photon interference. Numerical simulations identify the mean number of back-decays as a measurable quantity that correlates with achievable HOM visibility. Optimization of the excitation pulse with respect to a trade-off between photon yield and indistinguishability is analyzed. Finally, we compare the performance of different trapped-ion species for long-range dual-rail entanglement swapping via HOM photon interference.
summary: This theoretical study analyzes the indistinguishability of single photons emitted from trapped $^{40}	ext{Ca}^+$ ions via Raman scattering. It shows that spontaneous decay back to the initial state degrades the Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) interference visibility. The key finding is that the mean number of back-decays ($\langle N angle$) provides a measurable metric directly correlating with the achievable quantum interference visibility.
main_problem: The study investigates how spontaneous decay processes affect the indistinguishability of single Raman photons generated from trapped ions, which is crucial for quantum networking applications.
main_result: The mean number of back-decays ($\langle N angle$) is found to be a measurable quantity that directly correlates with the achievable Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) visibility, demonstrating a clear trade-off with photon yield.
method: The authors employ numerical simulations based on solving the master equation in Lindblad form, utilizing quantum jump decomposition to track decay paths.
model_or_system: The system involves single trapped $^{40}	ext{Ca}^+$ ions undergoing Raman scattering driven by few-nanosecond pulses, modeled as a three-level $\Lambda$-system. The dynamics are governed by a master equation incorporating spontaneous decay jump operators.
key_observables: HOM Visibility ($V$), Mean number of back-decays ($\langle N angle$), Probability of zero back-decays ($P_0$), and Raman photon success probability ($P_{	ext{Raman}}$).
important_parameters: Excitation pulse duration (few-nanosecond scale), decay rates ($\Gamma$), and the specific ion species ($^{40}	ext{Ca}^+$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the validity of the three-level model and the use of quantum jump decomposition to account for decay pathways.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the distributions of back-decay probabilities ($P_N$) for varying pulse lengths and demonstrate the quantitative correlation between $\langle N angle$ and $V_{	ext{HOM}}$ using derived inequalities.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework using the master equation and quantum jump decomposition. It then calculates key observables like $\langle N angle$ and $V_{	ext{HOM}}$, deriving explicit mathematical relationships between them. Finally, it extends the analysis to compare different trapped-ion species for long-range entanglement swapping.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to AMO physics and quantum optics as it tackles the fundamental decoherence mechanism (spontaneous decay) limiting the performance of solid-state and trapped-ion quantum memories and repeaters. The quantitative link between decay statistics and interference visibility is a key theoretical result.
